questions.q: A patient with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency develops haemolysis after exposure to an oxidant drug. Which red-cell function is impaired most directly?
options: Regeneration of reduced glutathione due to inadequate NADPH
questions.explain: The oxidative phase of the pentose phosphate pathway generates NADPH through G6PD. Red cells use NADPH to maintain glutathione in its reduced form, protecting haemoglobin and membranes from oxidant injury.

open.q: Why does G6PD deficiency predispose red cells to oxidative haemolysis?
accept: Reduced NADPH limits regeneration of reduced glutathione

questions.q: A patient develops bloating and osmotic diarrhoea after drinking milk. Symptoms improve when lactose is excluded. Which mechanism explains the diarrhoea?
options: Unabsorbed lactose retains water in the intestinal lumen and is fermented by colonic bacteria
Lactose directly stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate secretion
Glucose transport through SGLT1 is permanently blocked
Bile salts precipitate lactose in the ileum
questions.explain: Lactase deficiency leaves lactose in the intestinal lumen. Its osmotic effect draws water into the bowel, while bacterial fermentation produces gas and organic acids, causing bloating, flatulence and diarrhoea.

open.q: Explain how lactase deficiency causes osmotic diarrhoea and bloating.
accept: Unabsorbed lactose retains water osmotically and undergoes bacterial fermentation
Lactose remains in lumen, draws water and is fermented

questions.q: During glycogen synthesis, which activated glucose donor is used by glycogen synthase to elongate glycogen chains?
questions.explain: Glycogen synthase transfers glucose from UDP-glucose to the non-reducing ends of glycogen, forming alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds. UDP-glucose is generated from glucose-1-phosphate and UTP by UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase.

open.q: Which activated glucose donor is used by glycogen synthase?

questions.q: During prolonged fasting, hepatic gluconeogenesis uses lactate released by exercising skeletal muscle. Which cycle describes this transfer of carbon from muscle to liver and back to muscle?
questions.explain: In the Cori cycle, anaerobic glycolysis in muscle produces lactate, which travels to the liver and is converted to glucose by gluconeogenesis. Glucose returns to muscle for energy use; the liver expends ATP to support this recycling.

open.q: Describe the Cori cycle.
accept: Muscle-derived lactate is converted to glucose in the liver, which returns glucose to muscle
Lactate from muscle goes to liver for gluconeogenesis and glucose returns to muscle

questions.q: A 19-year-old man with recurrent fasting hypoglycaemia has impaired transport of long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondrial matrix. Which shuttle component is directly responsible for transferring the acyl group across the inner mitochondrial membrane?
questions.explain: Carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase exchanges acylcarnitine entering the matrix for free carnitine leaving it across the inner mitochondrial membrane. CPT I forms acylcarnitine at the outer membrane; CPT II regenerates acyl-CoA on the matrix side.

open.q: A 19-year-old man with recurrent fasting hypoglycaemia has impaired transport of long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondrial matrix. Which shuttle component is directly responsible for transferring the acyl group across the inner mitochondrial membrane?

questions.q: During prolonged fasting, hepatic ketogenesis rises. Which molecule is the immediate precursor formed by mitochondrial HMG-CoA lyase?
questions.explain: Mitochondrial HMG-CoA lyase cleaves HMG-CoA to form acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA. Acetoacetate can then be reduced to β-hydroxybutyrate or spontaneously decarboxylated to acetone.

open.q: During prolonged fasting, hepatic ketogenesis rises. Which molecule is the immediate precursor formed by mitochondrial HMG-CoA lyase?

questions.q: Which molecule provides the two-carbon units used by fatty acid synthase during de novo fatty acid synthesis?
questions.explain: Malonyl-CoA is generated from acetyl-CoA by acetyl-CoA carboxylase and donates two-carbon units during the fatty acid synthase elongation cycle, with decarboxylation driving condensation.

open.q: Which molecule provides the two-carbon units used by fatty acid synthase during de novo fatty acid synthesis?

questions.q: A patient with high hepatic lipogenesis has increased activity of acetyl-CoA carboxylase. Which metabolite directly inhibits this enzyme by feedback?
questions.explain: Long-chain fatty acyl-CoA, particularly palmitoyl-CoA, inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylase by feedback. Citrate is an allosteric activator, while insulin promotes its dephosphorylated active state.

open.q: A patient with high hepatic lipogenesis has increased activity of acetyl-CoA carboxylase. Which metabolite directly inhibits this enzyme by feedback?

questions.q: A patient with familial hypercholesterolaemia has markedly reduced hepatic LDL-receptor activity. Which change most directly explains the elevated plasma LDL concentration?
options: Reduced receptor-mediated uptake of LDL by hepatocytes
Increased conversion of LDL to bile acids in plasma
questions.explain: Hepatic LDL receptors remove circulating LDL by receptor-mediated endocytosis. Reduced receptor number or function decreases clearance and raises plasma LDL cholesterol.

open.q: A patient with familial hypercholesterolaemia has markedly reduced hepatic LDL-receptor activity. Which change most directly explains the elevated plasma LDL concentration?

questions.q: Which apolipoprotein is the principal activator of lipoprotein lipase on capillary endothelium?
questions.explain: ApoC-II activates lipoprotein lipase, which hydrolyses triacylglycerols in chylomicrons and VLDL. ApoE mediates remnant uptake and ApoA-I activates LCAT.

open.q: Which apolipoprotein is the principal activator of lipoprotein lipase on capillary endothelium?

questions.q: A patient taking low-dose aspirin has reduced platelet thromboxane A2 synthesis. Which enzyme is irreversibly acetylated by aspirin?
questions.explain: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclo-oxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin and thromboxane synthesis. Platelets cannot resynthesise COX, so the effect lasts for their lifespan.

open.q: A patient taking low-dose aspirin has reduced platelet thromboxane A2 synthesis. Which enzyme is irreversibly acetylated by aspirin?

questions.q: A child develops hypoketotic hypoglycaemia after an overnight fast. Which biochemical finding is most consistent with a defect in medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase?
options: Increased conversion of fatty acids to glucose
questions.explain: MCAD deficiency impairs mitochondrial β-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids. Incomplete oxidation produces characteristic medium-chain acylcarnitine accumulation, while reduced acetyl-CoA limits ketogenesis and contributes to hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

open.q: A child develops hypoketotic hypoglycaemia after an overnight fast. Which biochemical finding is most consistent with a defect in medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase?
